type: type-92 header-table record = one compiled script: owner header {+0x24 count, +0x28 capacity (== count), +0x2C 0x80000000|count*4, +0x30 -> own +0x34, +0x34.. count section-1 pointers}; the blob [entry, next entry) is tiled by the instruction records
structure: How a script is stored: an instruction-pointer array in the owner, instruction records after it

location.offset: all 157 type-92 header-table records of the tutorial (e.g. 027_HugoCS.ai at 0x2B633C: 204 pointers, 37 records, 0xE94 bytes)

meaning: Verified on 157/157 scripts (igz scripts): count == capacity, the size word is 0x80000000 | count*4, the array starts at +0x34 and the blob is fully tiled by records (0 uncovered bytes). Each pointer designates either a local instruction record (in the blob) or a shared record/value elsewhere (variables, attributes, array elements — arguments by reference; refcount-N records the header heuristic misses). An instruction record`s word +0 is its opcode CLASS (type index) and word +8 its opcode TEXT in section 2; 287 distinct opcodes in the tutorial ("parameter" 8 310, "set value||=" 7 140, "check value" 3 364, "set *reference||to" 2 274, "use macro" 1 052, "displace|||LENGTH:|HEADING:|PITCH:" 644, "clone||at|facing||cloned" 592, ...). The section-0 type names are therefore VM class names, not meanings: a "tfbSpriteInfo" (113) is a "set value" instruction, an "igIntKey" (100) a "parameter", a "ScriptSet" (111) a "set [set]", and "tfbPhysicsModel" (123) is the CLONE opcode class. Tool: igz script <decoded> <record> --fixups lists a script; igz scripts audits the model.
